@aio:claude-auth: ### Auth
Transport: **both**. `jwtAuth` (`src/middlewares/jwtAuth.ts`) checks the `accessToken`
cookie first, falling back to `Authorization: Bearer` — whichever the client actually sent.
`POST /api/v1/auth/login` and `/register` set httpOnly cookies (for browser clients) *and*
return `{ user, accessToken, refreshToken }` in the body (for bearer clients — mobile,
scripts). `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` takes an optional `{ refreshToken }` body: a bearer
client sends it, a cookie client omits it and the `refreshToken` cookie
(`path: "/api/v1/auth/refresh"`) is used instead. Either way the token is checked against
the SHA-256 hash stored on the user row (constant-time compare) and rotated with a
compare-and-swap (`updateMany` filtered by the hash just verified), so a stolen-and-replayed
old one is rejected once it's been rotated and two concurrent refreshes with the same token
can't both win. Never bcrypt for this hash: it only reads 72 bytes, the same prefix for every
JWT of a user — bcrypt is for passwords only. Every refresh token carries a random `jti`, so
two signed in the same second are still different. `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` (behind
`jwtAuth`) clears both cookies and the stored hash, revoking the session for every transport
at once.
**Client-side:** a browser consumer of `@{{scope}}/api-client` should still construct it
with `credentials: "include"` in `ApiClientConfig` to get the cookie path working; a
bearer consumer (mobile) just passes `accessToken`/`refreshToken` explicitly and can ignore
`credentials` entirely.
